artists.biography:
The Bluetones were an English indie rock band, formed in Hounslow, Greater London, in 1993. The band's members were Mark Morriss on vocals, Adam Devlin on guitar, Scott Morriss on bass guitar, and Eds Chesters on drums. A fifth member, Richard Payne, came on board between 1998 and 2002. The band was originally named "The Bottlegarden".

The Bluetones' commercial success waned after the fall of the Britpop movement, yet they continued to tour and release new records and were therefore often labelled as "Britpop survivors".

The band's final album A New Athens was released on 31 May 2010.

The band split on 1 October 2011 following a farewell tour which ended with a concert in Osaka, Japan.

perplexity.description:
Expecting to Fly is the debut studio album by British rock band The Bluetones, released on 12 February 1996 through Superior Quality Recordings and A&M Records. The album is a quintessential example of Britpop and indie pop, characterized by jangly guitar riffs, melodic hooks, and introspective lyrics. Drawing influence from classic British guitar pop and the emerging Britpop movement of the mid-1990s, the album features standout tracks such as "Bluetonic," "Slight Return," and "Cut Some Rug," which helped establish the band's reputation for catchy songwriting and accessible rock melodies.

As the band's first full-length release, Expecting to Fly marked The Bluetones' arrival on the UK music scene and quickly became a commercial success, reaching number one on the UK Albums Chart and displacing Oasis's What's the Story) Morning Glory? from the top spot. The album was certified Platinum by the BPI and received positive reviews for its polished production and consistent songcraft. It remains a defining work in The Bluetones' discography, setting the tone for their subsequent releases and solidifying their place within the Britpop era.
